versions.localizedDescription:
**Join any server. If you don't have the map, the game fetches it.**

This release makes internet multiplayer self-sufficient: joining a server that
runs a map you don't have no longer fails with an error — vkQuake offers to
download the map, installs it, and puts you in the game.

## Multiplayer map downloads

- **Join a server running a custom map you lack** and you get a prompt naming
  the map, its size, and where it comes from. Accept, watch the progress, and
  you're in — no leaving the app, no Files juggling.
- **Two community sources, tried in order:** the QuakeWorld community's bare-map
  mirror (maps.quakeworld.nu) for deathmatch maps, then the Quaddicted archive
  for single-player and co-op packages — with SHA-256 verification on archive
  packages.
- **Mid-game map rotation works too:** if the server changes to another map you
  lack, the same flow runs and rejoins you.
- **You stay in control:** Settings → Gameplay → Download Missing Maps
  (Never / Ask First / Always). Ask First is the default and always shows the
  size before using data. Downloads never overwrite files you already have.
- If a map exists on neither source, you get a clean message back to the menu
  instead of an error screen.

## Touch menus: scroll long lists by dragging

- **Drag anywhere on a long list** — the server browser, mods list, key
  bindings, or options — and it scrolls with your finger, one row per row.
  A tap only activates a row if your finger didn't move.
- **Tapping the scrollbar no longer activates a row** (on the server list this
  could join a server you never picked). A tap on the scrollbar itself now
  page-jumps instead.

### Install via SideStore source (recommended — auto-updates)
Add one URL to [SideStore](https://sidestore.io) / [AltStore](https://altstore.io) and vkQuake installs *and updates itself* when new versions ship:
- **iPhone / iPad:** `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rebelancap/quake-ports/main/apps-ios.json`
- **Apple Vision Pro:** `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rebelancap/quake-ports/main/apps-visionos.json`

These are shared sources — they also carry Quake II and Quake III. On **Apple Vision Pro**, first install SideStore onto the headset with [iloader](https://github.com/rebelancap/iloader/releases#release-visionos), then add the source in SideStore.

### Or download and sideload manually
- **`vkQuake-1.1.1-iOS.ipa`** — iPhone / iPad (iOS 16+)
- **`vkQuake-1.1.1-visionOS.ipa`** — Apple Vision Pro (visionOS 2+)

Full instructions in the [README](https://github.com/rebelancap/vkQuake-ios#readme).

## Notes

- The downloader covers maps. Servers that require a full client-side mod
  package (for example FTE/CSQC servers such as FortressOne) need engine
  features vkQuake does not provide — you can connect but only spectate.
- The visionOS build carries the same multiplayer changes; VR itself is
  unchanged from 1.1.0.

GPLv2, matching upstream vkQuake. QUAKE © id Software.

**Quake, at life scale, with a gun in each hand.** This release adds a full **VR mode** to the Vision Pro app, alongside the existing 2D window and 3D panel. Same app, same game data, same mods — switch modes from the ornament under the window.

## VR mode - **A real immersive space.** The Quake world surrounds you at life scale, head tracked, rendered per eye through the compositor's own matrices at the headset's native per-eye resolution. - **PSVR2 Sense controllers.** Aim with your hand, not a stick. The gun is where your hand is, points where you point it, and fires from its own barrel. - **Two guns at once.** In Immersive style each hand holds its own weapon and each trigger fires it, with a scheduler that keeps both firing while both triggers are held. - **Holsters.** Draw and stow from your hips. The belt follows your body when you walk and turn, and stays put when you merely glance over your shoulder. Click the left stick to clear both hips at once. - **Or don't.** Convenience style keeps the weapon in your hand at all times, no grip juggling, with stick-flick weapon cycling. - **A HUD you can read at a glance** — Quake's own status-bar face, armour plate and ammo boxes, on a small panel at a fixed distance, in High, Low or Off. - **The game's messages, in the world.** Locked-door messages, secrets, pickups and kill messages appear on a readable panel in front of you. - **Menus, console and save/load** appear on a world-locked screen inside the space, so everything the flat game can do, VR can do. - **Comfort.** Smooth turning by default (snap at 30/45/60 if you prefer), head-relative or controller-relative movement, automatic standing-height calibration with a trim in inches, recentre on the right stick click, and no camera motion you did not make with your own head. - **Per-hand haptics** for firing, holster entry, draw, stow and recentre. - **Gamepad-only VR works too**, aimed with your head. - **Mods work in VR.** Nothing here forks `progs.dat`, so Arcane Dimensions, Copper, the mission packs and the re-release campaigns all play in VR unmodified. - **Online multiplayer works in VR.** Join an ordinary NetQuake server and play it in the headset — the server sees a normal Quake client. (Dual wield is a local-server feature and steps aside on a remote server; you carry one weapon there, as usual.) - **A real settings screen** for all of it, which shows only the section for the mode you are actually in, with its own Reset. - **The Digital Crown is safe.** Pressing it leaves VR cleanly into the 2D window with your game paused and your settings saved — and the pause lifts the moment you move or fire. ## Also new outside VR - **PSVR2 Sense controllers now play the game in 2D and 3D mode**, not only in VR. Sticks move and look through the same response curves a gamepad uses, either trigger fires, A jumps, B sinks, the grips change weapon and MENU opens the menu. - **Ping in the multiplayer server list.** Every row shows its round-trip in milliseconds under a proper column header, and the list sorts lowest-ping-first. - **Joining a server whose map you don't have** now tells you so in plain language and returns you to the server list, instead of dropping you into a stack trace. (vkQuake has no content-download support, so the map still has to be one you own.) ## Fixed - **A latent crash on Vision Pro, present in every visionOS build since 1.0.5.** When the compositor declined to hand the app a frame — a system alert, an immersive-space transition, memory pressure — the 3D panel called a cleanup function on the already-invalidated frame, and the framework answers that with an abort rather than an error. It is a hard crash on any dropped frame, and it affected the **3D panel**, not only VR. Anyone using 3D mode should update. - **Dead triggers in VR.** The per-weapon refire clocks stored absolute server times, and server time restarts at zero on every level — so a timer saved late in one level landed far in the future in the next, and Quake stops reading weapon switches while such a timer is running. Both triggers could go dead until it expired, most often right at the start of a level. - **One gun turning into the other.** Holding the off hand's trigger re-rendered the aim hand's weapon as the firing gun, animation and all, because the engine's single view-model entity was pinned to the aim hand regardless of which hand was firing. - Weapon switching could put one shot through the wrong gun while both triggers were held. - Holstering your only weapon could leave it on the hip **and** in your hand. - Holster zones stayed pinned where you last recentred instead of following you. - Level transitions forgot your holsters and your off-hand weapon. - Standing height was computed through the world-scale setting, which made players shorter as the world got bigger. - The "are you sure?" confirmation could not be answered in 3D or VR, leaving the game stuck until relaunch. - Pressing the Digital Crown in VR could strand the app in a two-window state that needed a force-quit, and could leave a blank window behind afterwards. ## Notes - VR mode requires **visionOS 26 or later**. PSVR2 Sense controllers are optional but strongly recommended; without them VR is playable with a gamepad and head aim. - iPhone and iPad builds are unchanged by the VR work, apart from the server-list ping column and the friendlier missing-map message.

## Dawn of the Machine

Plays **Dawn of the Machine** — the new episode from the Quake 30th-anniversary update (2026-08-06), which installs as the `mg3` game directory. Upstream vkQuake still hard-crashes on it, so both fixes are carried here as overlay patches until upstream lands its own ([#980](https://github.com/Novum/vkQuake/issues/980), [#977](https://github.com/Novum/vkQuake/issues/977)).

**The crash.** `mg3` ships `progs/ogre_rocket.md5anim` with a joint count that disagrees with its mesh (39 vs 55), and the rocket ogre is precached by nearly every map — so the whole episode was unloadable, with `QUAKE ERROR: progs/ogre_rocket.md5anim has incorrect joint count`. It fires from the server's precache, so switching Models to classic did not avoid it either. That model now falls back to its classic `.mdl` and everything else keeps its enhanced mesh. All 20 `mg3` maps verified loading.

**Localized text.** The update moved the KEX strings out of `QuakeEX.kpf` — its `loc_*.txt` are now placeholders — and into `id1/pak0.pak`. Strings are read from the game paks now, so text works on both old and new rerelease data with nothing to configure.

If you updated your Quake install but copied only part of it across, old paks next to a new `QuakeEX.kpf` leaves no strings anywhere and everything renders as `$qc_item_health`. That combination now says so on the console instead of failing silently. The fix is to re-copy the whole `rerelease` folder — the anniversary patch rewrote every pak, not just the new episode's.

**Customizable touch layout.** *Settings → Touch Controls → Customize Touch Layout* — drag any control exactly where you want it, resize them all live with the slider, reset from the same bar. Your layout is saved per control.

The move stick is placeable too. It floats to wherever your thumb lands, so what it really has is an activation *zone* — shown in the editor as a large faint circle you can drag anywhere. # Quake III Arena 1.1.0 — VR on Apple Vision Pro

**Quake III Arena is now a full VR game on Apple Vision Pro.** Tap
**Enter VR** and you're standing inside the arena at real scale —
world-locked, head-tracked, running at native refresh on the headset.

## VR mode (Apple Vision Pro)

- **Full immersion** — the arena surrounds you; your head is the camera.
  Recenter any time; the Digital Crown always brings you home safely.
- **Three ways to aim:**
  - **Gaze aim** — the crosshair follows where you look. Zero setup;
    works with any gamepad for movement.
  - **Hand aim with PlayStation VR2 Sense controllers** — the gun is in
    your hand, with haptic feedback and per-weapon anchoring so every
    weapon points where you point.
  - **Gamepad aiming** — classic stick aiming: the stick turns your
    view and the crosshair stays dead center, exactly like flat Quake.
    (New "Aiming" setting appears when a regular gamepad is connected.)
- **A crosshair with real depth** — the aim marker sits in the world at
  the distance of whatever you're aiming at, and can never be swallowed
  by walls or clipped by geometry.
- **HUD and menus in-world** — drawn on a panel in front of you with
  size, height, and on/off controls; the scoreboard renders at one
  compact scale so full servers fit.
- **Comfort and image tuning** — snap or smooth turn, movement
  direction (head- or aim-relative), height calibration with trim,
  VR render quality up to 2× with live apply, CAS sharpening, Show
  Hands, and a damage-flash toggle.
- **Everything works in VR**: internet multiplayer (server browser,
  joining, auto-downloads), mods via drop-in folders (CPMA, OSP, Urban
  Terror, Team Arena), the single-player bot ladder, demos, cinematics.

## Urban Terror, fully online

Urban Terror now works end to end as a drop-in mod, on iPhone and
Vision Pro alike:

- **Account login works** — the engine now speaks Urban Terror's
  authentication protocol, so the auth-key screen appears and your
  account carries into servers.
- **The server browser fills up** — hundreds of live servers, with the
  master servers, per-server details, and the client identity all
  speaking UrT's dialect (generic Quake 3 clients get filtered or
  rejected; this port no longer looks like one to UrT).
- **Missing maps auto-download** from the server before joining, and
  big UrT maps load without memory errors.

## Keyboards & typing (iPhone & Vision Pro)

- Hardware keyboards now type into the game — console, player name,
  mod login fields (e.g. Urban Terror auth). Backtick opens the console.
- On iPhone, the game scales to fit above the on-screen keyboard so the
  field you're typing into stays visible; a **Paste** button on the
  keyboard bar pastes long strings like auth keys; Dismiss keeps the
  keyboard down until you tap back into a field.
- On Vision Pro, the on-screen keyboard appears automatically when a
  text field gets focus and leaves when you do; Mac Virtual Display
  keyboards route through natively.

## Gamepad: every button bindable

Every controller button now presses its own key, and all of them can be
rebound in your own `autoexec.cfg` — vanilla or any mod — to lay the
pad out exactly like your PC setup. Y, the d-pad, B, and R3 gained
dedicated keys (`AUX1`–`AUX7`); defaults are unchanged out of the box.
The full button→key table is in the README.

## Fixes and polish

- Weapon-switch names and the scoreboard no longer split or clip across
  HUD regions in VR.
- Switching mods mid-session no longer freezes the VR view.
- Backspace works everywhere text does.
- Assorted settings polish: cleaner Vision Pro VR section, sensible
  defaults dialed in on-device (Sharpen 50%, HUD height, weapon size,
  crosshair size), hardware clutter removed.

## Install

As always: sideload with SideStore / AltStore (on Vision Pro,
[iloader](https://github.com/rebelancap/iloader/releases#release-visionos)
installs SideStore), or grab the IPA below. You bring your own Quake III
game files — see the README.

*Built on [Quake3e](https://github.com/ec-/Quake3e) (Vulkan renderer on
Metal via MoltenVK). GPL v2.*

**Quake III Arena for iPhone, iPad, and Apple Vision Pro** — a native port of [Quake3e](https://github.com/ec-/Quake3e), the performance-focused ioquake3 fork, with its Vulkan renderer running on MoltenVK.

Ships with **no game content** — you supply your own Quake III Arena data (`baseq3` from any purchase).

### What's new in 1.0.4

**Other app audio.** *Settings → Audio* now decides what happens to music or a podcast that is already playing when you start a match:

- **Stop Other Audio** — they stop when Quake3e starts.
- **Play Both** — both at full volume, neither one quieter.
- **Lower Other Audio** *(the new default)* — they drop to the background, game audio stays full.
- **Lower Game Audio** — the game drops to the background while they play.
- **Mute Game Audio** — the game goes silent while they play, and comes back when they stop.

The last two are not something iOS will do for you — it lowers *other* apps on request, never you — so the game attenuates its own mix, fading rather than cutting, and the music keeps advancing while it is quiet. Every option in the picker says what it does in a sentence.

**Master volume.** One slider above Sound and Music that pulls everything down together — effects, music, cinematics. It deliberately sits outside the engine's volume cvars, so it is never written into your config and never fights the Sound Volume slider in the stock menus.

**Touch controls scale completely.** The controls size slider only ever grew the rings: the crosshair, the arrows and the weapon triangles inside them stayed the size they always were, and the floating move stick, its nub and the ≡/⚙ buttons never scaled at all. Now everything follows the one slider, and the glyphs stay sharp at the top of the range.

The move stick's activation zone scales with it too — so shrinking the controls also shrinks the area where your thumb summons the stick. Its circle is drawn in *Customize Touch Layout*, where you can see exactly what you are getting and drag it wherever you like.

Also: the layout editor's own size slider no longer drops the yellow outlines while you drag it, and it and the settings sheet finally agree on the same range.

- **Lobby queries time out** instead of hanging indefinitely, and **Refresh no longer locks up permanently** when a query fails to start.
- **Each install now has a stable network id.** iOS masks the hardware address, which had been collapsing every device's coopnet fingerprint to the same value.

- **Lower Other Audio** — music and podcasts drop to the background; game audio stays full *(default)*
- **Lower Game Audio** — game audio drops to the background while another app is playing
- **Mute Game Audio** — game audio goes silent while another app is playing

Each option explains itself in the picker, so you don't have to guess which side
gets quieter. The last two fade over about a fifth of a second rather than cutting,
and they sit on top of the game's own Music and Sound sliders — the in-game options
keep working and are never overwritten by the ducking.

There's a master **Game volume** slider in the same section.

### If you play with music going

Two things changed from earlier builds. Apotris used to mix with other audio at full
volume and follow the ring/silent switch; it now uses the audio category those five
modes need. So by default other audio is **lowered** while you play — pick **Play
Both** for the old behaviour — and game sound keeps playing with the ring/silent
switch off. Turn Game volume down if you want it quiet.

### Also

- Sound comes back after a phone call or Siri interrupts it. Previously the audio
  stayed dead until you left the app and came back.

### Pick up where you left off

Leaving the app now saves your run, so a force-quit — or a reboot, or iOS
evicting the app — no longer loses a long game. **Continue** appears at the top
of the main menu on the next launch and puts you back exactly where you were:
board, active piece, hold, next queue, score, level, timer and grade progress.

Backgrounding on its own never ended a run (the game just pauses in place), so
this only kicks in when the app actually stops running.

One slot, and it's cleared once you resume — a run you carried to a game over
can't be reloaded and re-rolled onto the leaderboards.
